verdicts.note: Reproduced exactly. 6,000 Codex threads have an agent-workspace cwd; 4,812 have source.subagent.thread_spawn (80.2%). aiur: 949 top-level (830 aiur-team/aiur + 106 its-everdred/aiur + 13 flat dirs #1471-#1687 that resolve to aiur-team/aiur) and 3,529 spawned (3,265 + 197 + 67). 3,529/949 = 3.72. Totals: Codex 1,188 + Claude 1,278 + opencode 2 = 2,468 top-level; 4,812 + 375 = 5,187 subagent. At ~19:00Z the live Claude counts had grown to 1,299 / 376 (khala only), which is consistent with the report's snapshot note. Attribution is sound: all 4,812 spawned threads have a parent thread in the SAME cwd (4,785 depth 1 with a top-level parent, 27 depth 2), so no subagent is counted against the wrong ticket or backend. Caveats that do not overturn the claim: (1) the example path shape is slightly wrong. The dominant form is /root/review_<name> (2,468 threads, e.g. review_correctness 415). /root/<name>_review has 302 threads. The review family is about 60% of spawns and simplify_* about 13%. (2) Only 598 of 1,188 top-level Codex agent threads spawn at all, so the fan-out is about 8 per spawning thread, not a uniform 3.7-4. (3) Thread count is not cost. On aiur, spawned threads used 33.7B of 50.2B total tokens (67%) and 86M of 118M output tokens (73%). That is 2.0x to 2.7x the top-level usage, not 3.7x. The load-bearing statement that a model is 'off by about 4x' is true for thread or concurrency counts but overstates the cost error. (4) The 2,468 / 5,187 totals mix windows: Codex from 2026-07-16, Claude about 30 days. The subagent share is backend-specific: Codex 80%, Claude 23% (375 of 1,653).

verdicts.method: gh api 'repos/aiur-team/<r>/issues/events?per_page=100' --paginate --jq '.[]|select(.event=="labeled" or .event=="unlabeled" or .event=="closed" or .event=="reopened")|{id,event,label:.label.name,n:.issue.number,pr:(.issue.pull_request!=null),actor:.actor.login,t:.created_at}' for aiur, archon and khala (saved to /home/everdred/.aiur/research/refactor-2026-09-26/scratch/resume-census2/events_<r>.jsonl), then my own Python counts. I also computed the per-issue distribution, the transition pairs from time-ordered labeled events, and the window-truncation check.
verdicts.note: Reproduced. aiur window is 2026-07-17T03:05Z to 09-26 (truncated by the 30,000-event cap). There are 10,822 agent:* labeled events, but 12 of them are on 5 PRs, so they fall on 688 issues+PRs. Issue-only: 10,810 events on 683 issues, 15.83 per issue. That explains the 'inconsistency': the table total 10,822 includes the 12 PR events, and the per-issue figure, the actor split (7,068 / 2,099 / 1,643, which sums to 10,810) and ci-wait 2,708 are issue-only. With PR events included, the figures are 7,077 / 2,100 / 1,645 and ci-wait 2,710. rework is 2,873 on either base. The difference is immaterial. archon: 972 / 93 = 10.45. khala at the snapshot: 2,267 / 214 = 10.59; live now 2,325 / 222 = 10.47. The churn is broad, not a few pathological tickets: median 12 events per issue, p90 32, max 116. The top 10% of issues (68) carry 33% of events. 481 of 683 issues had at least one rework and 542 had at least one ci-wait. The dominant loops are ci-wait<->in-progress (1,409 + 1,168 transitions) and rework<->ci-wait (1,229 + 1,109). Caveats: (1) 630 of the 2,873 rework events re-apply rework directly after rework (160 issues, 200 of them within 1 minute, one issue 58 times). That is label flapping, not new review cycles, so 'rework loops' overstates review round-trips by up to about 22%. (2) Overlay labels (paused 232, rate-limit-fallback 71, error 233) are counted as churn although they are not state transitions. (3) Truncation lowers the average slightly: 650 of 683 issues start with agent:todo inside the window, and their mean is 16.25. (4) Actor is not role. its-applekid is both the agent identity and the daemon's PAT identity, and aiur-daemon[bot] made no label writes after 2026-09-16. So 'its-applekid applied 7,068' does not mean agents applied them.

verdicts.method: Same REST event pull as census-05, plus gh api 'repos/aiur-team/<r>/issues?state=all&per_page=100' --paginate --jq '.[]|{n:.number,pr:(.pull_request!=null),state,reason:.state_reason,closed_at,labels:[.labels[].name]}' for aiur, khala and archon (/home/everdred/.aiur/research/refactor-2026-09-26/scratch/resume-census2/issues_<r>.jsonl). Per issue, I replayed the labels up to the last close and checked the agent:* labeled/unlabeled events within 1 h after it, split before and after 2026-09-17. I compared agent:done writes and closes by day. I read the snapshot code src/lib/aiur/github/issue_state.ex (swap_labels, remove_active_state_labels, handle_closed_active_target), state_policy.ex and orchestrator/merged_ticket_reconciler.ex. I ran git log on those files and grepped terminal_states in the aiur, archon and global ~/.aiur/config.
verdicts.note: The facts reproduce. khala has 6 agent:done labeled events (all by its-everdred), and 49 of 214 ever-labeled issues carry an agent:* label at the snapshot (live now: 50 of 222). aiur has 564 issues that carry agent:done now. But the per-repo reading is confounded by time. agent:done writes stopped on every repo in mid-September: aiur's last was 2026-09-16 and archon's last was 09-11. aiur has 40 closes after 09-16 with 0 agent:done. khala's first issue is dated 09-16, so almost its whole life falls after that change. aiur tickets closed from 2026-09-17 behave like khala's. Of 35 closes with an active agent:* label at close, 21 had the active label stripped within 1 h (same as khala's 185 of 190), none got agent:done, and the 14 kept were mostly paused or todo tickets closed by hand. Before 09-17, done was mostly written AFTER the merge-close: by aiur-daemon[bot] (167 aiur, 75 archon) or by its-applekid (81 aiur). The bot identity made no label writes on any repo after 09-16. The divergence is not in config or code. aiur, archon and the global config all list done in terminal_states. The terminal-label code is shared: remove_active_state_labels preserves terminal labels, and handle_closed_active_target strips active labels from a closed issue. issue_state.ex and merged_ticket_reconciler.ex have not changed since 2026-08-24. So agent:done 'stays' in both repos once written (khala's 6 are still there). The difference is whether done gets written at all, and that depends on when the ticket closed, not on which repo it is in. The cause of the mid-September stop is not verified. It coincides with the end of aiur-daemon[bot] label writes on 09-16.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The meaning of 'currently labeled' changes by era, not by repo. Up to about 2026-09-16, aiur and archon tickets usually got agent:done after the merge-close, mostly written by aiur-daemon[bot], and those labels persist: aiur has 564 and archon 82. From 2026-09-17 on, no repo gets agent:done on close (aiur 0 of 40 closes; khala 6 of 194, all added by hand). Instead, the active agent:* label is stripped within about 1-2 minutes of the close: 21 of 35 actively-labeled aiur closes and 185 of 190 khala closes. khala (created 09-16) exists only in the new era, so 49 of 214 ever-labeled issues are labeled now. The config (terminal_states includes done) and the terminal-label code are the same for all repos. A metric that reads current labels is therefore wrong for every repo after mid-September, and a state-model refactor faces one changed convention over time, not two per-repo conventions. The cause of the change is unverified. It coincides with the GitHub App identity's last label write on 2026-09-16.
